```{r setup, include=FALSE}
}
```

```{r load-stadester-json, include=FALSE}
regs_list <- sdata$regions

fmt_eu_pop <- function (arg0_val) {
  if (is.null(arg0_val) || is.na(arg0_val)) return("-")
  v <- as.numeric(arg0_val)
  if (v <= 0) return("-")
  if (v >= 1000000) {
    m <- round(v / 1000000, 2)
    s <- gsub("\\.", ",", format(m, nsmall = 2, trim = TRUE))
    s <- sub(",?0+$", "", s)
    return(paste0(s, "M"))
  }
  if (v >= 1000) {
    k <- round(v / 1000, 1)
    s <- gsub("\\.", ",", format(k, nsmall = 1, trim = TRUE))
    s <- sub(",?0+$", "", s)
    return(paste0(s, "k"))
  }
  return(as.character(as.integer(round(v))))
}

fmt_eu_coord <- function (arg0_x) {
  s <- format(round(as.numeric(arg0_x), 2), nsmall = 2, trim = TRUE)
  s <- gsub("\\.", ",", s)
  sub(",?0+$", "", s)
}

hyphenate_long_name <- function (arg0_str) {
  if (is.null(arg0_str) || is.na(arg0_str) || !nzchar(arg0_str)) return(arg0_str)
  s <- arg0_str
  s <- gsub("Dnipropetrovsk", "Dnipropet-rovsk", s, fixed = TRUE)
  s <- gsub("Dnepropetrovsk", "Dnepropet-rovsk", s, fixed = TRUE)
  s <- gsub("Dneprodzerzhinsk", "Dneprodzer-zhinsk", s, fixed = TRUE)
  s <- gsub("Dniprodzerzhynsk", "Dniprodzer-zhynsk", s, fixed = TRUE)
  s <- gsub("Voroshilovgrad", "Voroshilov-grad", s, fixed = TRUE)
  s <- gsub("Voroshylovhrad", "Voroshylov-hrad", s, fixed = TRUE)
  s <- gsub("Medvezhyegorsk", "Medvezhye-gorsk", s, fixed = TRUE)
  s <- gsub("Medvezhegorsk", "Medvezhe-gorsk", s, fixed = TRUE)
  s <- gsub("Krasnoturyinsk", "Krasnotur-yinsk", s, fixed = TRUE)
  s <- gsub("Blagoveshchensk", "Blagovesh-chensk", s, fixed = TRUE)
  s <- gsub("Novoshakhtinsk", "Novoshakh-tinsk", s, fixed = TRUE)
  s <- gsub("Konstantinovka", "Konstanti-novka", s, fixed = TRUE)
  s <- gsub("Yekaterinoslav", "Yekaterino-slav", s, fixed = TRUE)
  s <- gsub("Krasnoarmeyskaya", "Krasnoarmey-skaya", s, fixed = TRUE)
  s <- gsub("Chernyakhovsk", "Chernyak-hovsk", s, fixed = TRUE)
  s <- gsub("Krasnoarmeysk-Volga", "Krasno-armeysk-Volga", s, fixed = TRUE)
  gsub("([A-Za-z]{8})([A-Za-z]{6,})", "\\1-\\2", s)
}

get_entry_pop <- function (arg0_entry, arg1_yr_str) {
  p <- arg0_entry$population[[arg1_yr_str]]
  if (is.null(p)) return(NA_real_)
  as.numeric(p)
}

get_occupied_span <- function (arg0_entry) {
  yrs <- as.integer(names(arg0_entry$population))
  if (length(yrs) == 0) return("-")
  paste0(min(yrs), "-", max(yrs))
}

build_reg_df <- function (arg0_reg_nums) {
  idx_vec <- which(entry_reg_nums %in% arg0_reg_nums)
  sub_list <- all_entries[idx_vec]
  sub_regs <- entry_reg_nums[idx_vec]
  rows <- lapply(seq_along(sub_list), function (i) {
    e <- sub_list[[i]]
    rnum <- sub_regs[i]
    raw_oth <- if (length(e$other_names) > 0) unlist(e$other_names) else character(0)
    oth <- if (length(raw_oth) > 0) paste(head(raw_oth, 2L), collapse = "; ") else "-"
    coords_span <- paste0(
      fmt_eu_coord(e$coords[[1]]), ", ", fmt_eu_coord(e$coords[[2]]),
      " (", get_occupied_span(e), ")"
    )
    data.frame(
      `Settlement` = paste0(hyphenate_long_name(e$name), " (Reg. ", rnum, ")"),
      `Other Names` = hyphenate_long_name(oth),
      `Coords` = coords_span,
      `1926` = fmt_eu_pop(get_entry_pop(e, "1926")),
      `1933` = fmt_eu_pop(get_entry_pop(e, "1933")),
      `1939` = fmt_eu_pop(get_entry_pop(e, "1939")),
      `1945` = fmt_eu_pop(get_entry_pop(e, "1945")),
      `1953` = fmt_eu_pop(get_entry_pop(e, "1953")),
      check.names = FALSE,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  })
  do.call(rbind, rows)
}
```

# Abstract

Between the First All-Union Census of December 1926 and the death of Joseph Stalin in March 1953, the urban network of the European and Asian Soviet Union was transformed by Five-Year-Plan industrialisation, wartime devastation and the expansion of the Gulag. Across the 251 towns, republic capitals, industrial centres and forced-labour camp settlements covered in this gazetteer, the combined urban population more than doubled from 16,91M in 1926 to 41,18M in 1953. Rapid industrial construction in the 1930s and factory evacuations during the Second World War multiplied the size of Moscow, Gorky and the coal and steel cities of the Donbas, the Urals, the Kuzbass and Western Siberia, while creating entirely new polar mining and port towns at Vorkuta, Norilsk, Igarka and Magadan.

Over the same quarter-century, war, genocide and forced migration hollowed out the historic cities of the western borderlands and the occupied front zone. Between 1941 and 1945, the Holocaust annihilated the Jewish urban communities of Vilnius, Kaunas, Riga, Minsk, Vitebsk, Lviv, Kyiv and Odesa, siege and combat reduced Leningrad, Stalingrad, Voronezh, Sevastopol and Narva to rubble and post-war population transfers replaced the pre-war inhabitants of Kaliningrad, Vyborg, Klaipeda and Yuzhno-Sakhalinsk.

# Methodology

This gazetteer traces the population of 251 towns, republic capitals, Five-Year-Plan industrial boomtowns and Gulag camp centres across the 45 Stalin-era regions of Estonia (Region 1, 6 towns), Latvia (Region 2, 6 towns), Lithuania (Region 3, 5 towns), Moldova (Region 4, 6 towns), Belarus (Regions 6-7, 18 towns), Ukraine including Crimea (Regions 8-15, 63 towns) and Russia including Kaliningrad Oblast and Karelia (Region 5 and Regions 16-45, 147 towns) at five benchmark dates: 1926, 1933, 1939, 1945 and 1953.

Population figures for 1926 and 1939 come from the All-Union Censuses of 17 December 1926 and 17 January 1939, supplemented for the borderland cities annexed between 1939 and 1945 (Tallinn, Tartu, Narva and Parnu in Region 1; Riga, Liepaja, Daugavpils and Jelgava in Region 2; Vilnius, Kaunas, Klaipeda and Siauliai in Region 3; Chisinau, Balti and Bender in Region 4; Kaliningrad/Konigsberg, Sovetsk/Tilsit and Chernyakhovsk/Insterburg in Region 5; Brest and Grodno in Region 6; Lviv, Ternopil and Lutsk in Region 8; Chernivtsi, Izmail and Uzhhorod in Region 9; Vyborg and Sortavala in Region 16; Kyzyl in Region 39; and Yuzhno-Sakhalinsk/Toyohara in Region 45) by Estonian, Latvian, Lithuanian, Polish, Romanian, Czechoslovak, Finnish, German, Tuvan and Japanese censuses [@tsunkhu1929perepis1926; @polyakov1992perepis1939; @andreev1998demograficheskaya; @parming1972estonia; @zvidrins1992latvia; @balkelis2005vilnius; @kostyashov2009sekretnaya]. Estimates for 1933, 1945 and 1953 are drawn from urban registration books, Evacuation Council and post-liberation municipal counts (1944-1945), NKVD-MVD camp and special-settlement files and statistical yearbooks [@polyakov1991perepis1937; @rudnytskyi2015holodomor; @zemskov2003spetsposelentsy; @khlevniuk2004history; @casu2014moldova]. Benchmarks before a settlement's foundation (such as Kohtla-Jarve, Sillamae, Vorkuta, Inta, Norilsk, Magadan, Susuman or Pevek in 1926) or after its wartime destruction (Khatyn after March 1943) are marked with a hyphen (`-`).

# Results

## Regions 1 - 5: Baltic SSRs, Moldavian SSR and Kaliningrad Oblast

Table \ref{tab:reg1-5} gives the population of 28 towns across Estonia (Region 1), Latvia (Region 2), Lithuania (Region 3), Moldova (Region 4) and Kaliningrad Oblast (Region 5) [@mertelsmann2009estonia; @strods2002priboi; @balkelis2005vilnius; @casu2014moldova; @kostyashov2022kaliningrad].

```{r table-reg1-5, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
render_table_template(
  build_reg_df(1:5),
  list(
    caption = "Town populations across Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Moldova and Kaliningrad Oblast (Regions 1 to 5) at the 1926, 1933, 1939, 1945 and 1953 benchmarks, showing wartime losses in Riga, Vilnius and Konigsberg/Kaliningrad and the post-war creation of Estonian oil-shale and uranium towns.",
    label = "tab:reg1-5"
  )
)
```

## Regions 6 - 7: Western and Eastern Belarus

Table \ref{tab:reg6-7} covers 18 settlements across Western Belarus (Region 6: Brest, Grodno, Baranovichi, Molodechno, Pinsk and Lida) and Eastern Belarus (Region 7: Minsk, Vitebsk, Gomel, Mogilev, Bobruisk, Polotsk, Orsha, Borisov, Mozyr, Slutsk, Rechitsa and the razed village of Khatyn) [@bylov2004belarus; @arad2009holocaust].

```{r table-reg6-7, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
render_table_template(
  build_reg_df(6:7),
  list(
    caption = "Town populations across Western and Eastern Belarus (Regions 6 and 7) from 1926 to 1953, capturing the destruction of Jewish urban communities in Minsk, Vitebsk, Brest and Pinsk between 1941 and 1944 and post-war industrial rebuilding.",
    label = "tab:reg6-7"
  )
)
```

## Regions 8 - 11: Western, Right-Bank and Left-Bank Ukraine

Table \ref{tab:reg8-11} presents 38 towns across Galicia and Volhynia (Region 8), Northern Bukovina, Budjak and Transcarpathia (Region 9), Right-Bank Ukraine (Region 10) and Left-Bank Ukraine (Region 11) [@rudnytskyi2015holodomor; @wolowyna2020holodomor; @polian2001against].

```{r table-reg8-11, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
render_table_template(
  build_reg_df(8:11),
  list(
    caption = "Town populations across Western, Right-Bank and Left-Bank Ukraine (Regions 8 to 11) from 1926 to 1953, reflecting the 1933 famine in Kharkiv and Poltava, the wartime depopulation of Kyiv and Lviv and the Polish-Ukrainian population exchanges.",
    label = "tab:reg8-11"
  )
)
```

## Regions 12 - 15: Dnieper Bend, Donbas, Black Sea Steppe and Crimea

Table \ref{tab:reg12-15} covers 25 towns across the Dnieper Industrial Bend (Region 12), the Donbas Coal-Metallurgical Basin (Region 13), the Ukrainian Black Sea Steppe (Region 14) and Crimea (Region 15) [@polyakov1992perepis1939; @senyavsky2019urbanisation; @bugai1995deportatsiya].

```{r table-reg12-15, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
render_table_template(
  build_reg_df(12:15),
  list(
    caption = "Town populations across the Dnieper Bend, Donbas, Black Sea Steppe and Crimea (Regions 12 to 15) from 1926 to 1953, contrasting rapid Five-Year-Plan growth in Zaporizhzhia, Kryvyi Rih and Stalino with wartime ruin and the 1944 Crimean Tatar deportation.",
    label = "tab:reg12-15"
  )
)
```

## Regions 16 - 22: Karelia, Leningrad, Komi, Moscow and Central Russia

Table \ref{tab:reg16-22} lists 42 settlements across Karelia and Murmansk (Region 16), Leningrad, Novgorod and Pskov (Region 17), the Komi ASSR and Nenets Okrug (Region 18), Arkhangelsk and Vologda (Region 19), Moscow (Region 20), the Upper Volga and Western Front (Region 21) and the Central Black-Earth Belt (Region 22) [@baron2007karelia; @lomagin2002neizvestnaya; @applebaum2003gulag].

```{r table-reg16-22, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
render_table_template(
  build_reg_df(16:22),
  list(
    caption = "Town populations across Karelia, Leningrad, Komi, Moscow and Central Russia (Regions 16 to 22) from 1926 to 1953, showing the 1941-1944 siege collapse of Leningrad and Novgorod alongside the rapid rise of Moscow and the Arctic coal camps of Vorkuta and Inta.",
    label = "tab:reg16-22"
  )
)
```

## Regions 23 - 34: Volga-Ural Republics, North Caucasus and the Urals

Table \ref{tab:reg23-34} covers 54 towns across the Volga-Vyatka and Middle Volga republics (Regions 23-25), the liquidated Volga German and Kalmyk ASSRs (Regions 26 and 28), the Lower Volga and North Caucasus (Regions 27 and 29-33) and the Ural industrial region and Bashkir ASSR (Region 34) [@german2000nemtsy; @bugai1995deportatsiya; @tsutsiev2014atlas; @kotkin1995magnetic].

```{r table-reg23-34, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
render_table_template(
  build_reg_df(23:34),
  list(
    caption = "Town populations across the Volga-Ural republics, Lower Volga, North Caucasus and the Urals (Regions 23 to 34) from 1926 to 1953, contrasting the wartime depopulation of Stalingrad, Engels, Elista and Grozny with booming evacuation and steel cities in the Urals.",
    label = "tab:reg23-34"
  )
)
```

## Regions 35 - 45: Siberia, the Arctic Gulag and the Far East

Table \ref{tab:reg35-45} presents 46 towns and camp settlements across Western Siberia and the Kuzbass (Regions 35-38), the Altai-Sayan republics (Region 39), Eastern Siberia and the Yenisei-Taymyr polar zone (Regions 40-41), Buryatia, Chita and Yakutia (Regions 42-43), the Dalstroy Kolyma-Magadan complex (Region 44) and the Southern Far East (Region 45) [@werth2007cannibal; @shalak2005eastsiberia; @antonov2018churapcha; @applebaum2003gulag].

```{r table-reg35-45, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
render_table_template(
  build_reg_df(35:45),
  list(
    caption = "Town populations across Western and Eastern Siberia, the Arctic Gulag and the Far East (Regions 35 to 45) from 1926 to 1953, showing the expansion of Novosibirsk, Omsk, Stalinsk, Norilsk, Magadan and Komsomolsk-on-Amur.",
    label = "tab:reg35-45"
  )
)
```

# Appendix

## Regional Gazetteer Summary

Table \ref{tab:regional-summary} sums the population of the 251 towns across each of the 45 regions at the five benchmark dates between 1926 and 1953.

```{r table-summary, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}

  "2. Latvian SSR",

  "33. Dagestan ASSR",

  "36. Ob-Irtysh Taiga (Narym, Yugra, Yamal)",
  "37. Kuzbass Coal-Steel Basin",
  "38. Altai Krai",
  "39. Gorno-Altai, Khakass & Tuva AOs",

  "41. Yenisei-Taymyr Polar Zone (Norilsk)",
  "42. Buryat-Mongol ASSR & Chita",
  "43. Yakut ASSR",
  "44. Kolyma-Magadan, Chukotka & Kamchatka",
  "45. Southern Far East & Sakhalin"
)
bench_yrs <- c("1926", "1933", "1939", "1945", "1953")

sum_rows <- lapply(1:45, function (rnum) {
  idx <- which(entry_reg_nums == rnum)
  sub_e <- all_entries[idx]
  sums <- sapply(bench_yrs, function (y) {
    vals <- sapply(sub_e, function (e) {
      v <- get_entry_pop(e, y)
      if (is.na(v)) 0 else v
    })
    fmt_eu_pop(sum(vals))
  })
  data.frame(
    `Region (Towns)` = paste0(short_reg_names[rnum], " (", length(idx), ")"),
    `1926` = sums[["1926"]],
    `1933` = sums[["1933"]],
    `1939` = sums[["1939"]],
    `1945` = sums[["1945"]],
    `1953` = sums[["1953"]],
    check.names = FALSE,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})
df_sum <- do.call(rbind, sum_rows)

tot_sums <- sapply(bench_yrs, function (y) {
  vals <- sapply(all_entries, function (e) {
    v <- get_entry_pop(e, y)
    if (is.na(v)) 0 else v
  })
  fmt_eu_pop(sum(vals))
})
tot_row <- data.frame(
  `Region (Towns)` = paste0("All 45 Regions (", length(all_entries), " towns)"),
  `1926` = tot_sums[["1926"]],
  `1933` = tot_sums[["1933"]],
  `1939` = tot_sums[["1939"]],
  `1945` = tot_sums[["1945"]],
  `1953` = tot_sums[["1953"]],
  check.names = FALSE,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
df_sum <- rbind(df_sum, tot_row)

render_table_template(
  df_sum,
  list(
    caption = "Combined urban population of the 251 towns across all 45 regions from 1926 to 1953, showing the doubling of the urban network over the Stalin era despite wartime devastation in the occupied west.",
    label = "tab:regional-summary"
  )
)
```
